arguments.name: M1.1 Define customer CSV data contract & schema registry
arguments.details:
Document the inbound CSV contract: required/optional columns, types, allowed value domains, nullability, encoding, delimiter/quoting rules, max row/file size, and PII classification per field.

Deliverables: versioned schema definitions in the registry, a written data contract doc, and a sample-file fixture set covering valid, malformed, and edge-case files (embedded commas, newlines in quotes, BOM, UTF-8 vs Latin-1, duplicate headers).

Acceptance: contract reviewed and signed off by the dashboard consumers and the CSV source owners; fixtures committed and reusable by tests downstream.

arguments.name: M1.2 Stand up CSV landing zone & file intake
arguments.details:
Create the object-storage landing zone with raw/processing/archive prefixes, a manifest table that records each arriving file (name, size, checksum, source, received_at), and an intake process that detects new files and registers them.

Deliverables: bucket/prefix layout as code, manifest schema, file-arrival trigger, retention policy for archived files, access policy limiting write access to the intake role only.

Acceptance: dropping a new CSV into the landing zone creates exactly one manifest row; re-dropping an identical checksum is flagged rather than reprocessed. Out of scope: parsing and validation logic (M1.3).

arguments.name: M1.3 Build CSV parser & validation rule engine
arguments.details:
Implement streaming CSV parsing against the M1.1 contract with a declarative, config-driven rule engine so new rules do not require code changes.

Cover: type coercion, required-field presence, enum/domain checks, range checks, regex checks, cross-field consistency, and row-level error capture with column, rule id, and raw value.

Deliverables: parser module, rule definitions file, unit tests per rule type, and a documented way to add a rule. Process files in chunks so a large file does not exhaust memory.

Acceptance: all M1.1 fixtures produce the expected pass/fail outcome per row; malformed rows never crash the job; parse throughput meets the agreed file-size budget.

arguments.name: M1.4 Implement dedupe & idempotent load semantics
arguments.details:
Define a stable natural/business key for customer records and an idempotency key for each load batch. Implement upsert (merge) semantics so replaying the same file produces no duplicates and no unintended updates.

Deliverables: key derivation logic, dedupe strategy (in-batch plus cross-batch), soft-delete handling, and a documented replay procedure.

Acceptance: running the same file twice leaves row counts unchanged; a corrected re-delivery of an existing customer updates rather than duplicates; concurrent loads of the same file cannot create duplicate rows (verified by test).

arguments.name: M1.5 Normalize customers into canonical model
arguments.details:
Map source columns to the canonical customer entity: split/merge name fields, standardize email and phone formats, normalize country/region/currency codes to ISO, parse dates to UTC, and resolve identity across sources (email plus stable external id) into a single customer record with source lineage.

Deliverables: transformation logic, mapping table from source field to canonical field, collision/conflict resolution rules, and lineage columns (source_file, ingested_at).

Acceptance: normalized output validates against the canonical schema; a customer appearing in two files resolves to one record with deterministic conflict resolution; unit tests cover locale and date-format edge cases.

arguments.name: M1.6 Build quarantine store & data quality reporting
arguments.details:
Route rejected/partial rows to a quarantine store with the failing rule, raw payload, and source file, plus a reprocess path once the source is fixed.

Deliverables: quarantine table with status (new/fixed/ignored), reprocess utility, and data quality metrics — rows in/out, reject rate by rule and by source, freshness, schema-drift warnings — exposed for the M4 dashboards.

Acceptance: every rejected row is explainable from the quarantine record; fix-and-reprocess moves a row out of quarantine correctly; DQ metrics queryable with <5s latency.

arguments.name: M1.7 Add incremental load & backfill orchestration
arguments.details:
Wrap the ingestion pieces (intake → parse → validate → dedupe → normalize) in an orchestrated, scheduled workflow with retries, alerting on failure, and a parameterized backfill mode for historical files.

Deliverables: orchestration DAG/job definitions, watermark/checkpoint logic for incremental runs, backfill runbook, retry and dead-letter behavior.

Acceptance: scheduled run processes only new files; a 12-month backfill completes within the window and is safely resumable after interruption; failed runs raise an alert and can be re-run without duplication.

arguments.name: M2.1 Define log event schema & field taxonomy
arguments.details:
Agree the canonical log event: timestamp (UTC), service, environment, level, logger, message, trace/request id, user/customer id, latency, status code, error type/stack hash, plus a taxonomy of event names and error categories used by the dashboard.

Deliverables: schema doc, enum values for level/error category, guidance for app teams on emitting structured JSON logs, and a backward-compatibility note for existing plaintext formats.

Acceptance: schema approved by the app engineering leads; every field the dashboard needs is sourced from this schema (no ad hoc parsing in the UI).

arguments.name: M2.2 Collect application logs into central store
arguments.details:
Wire application log shipping into the central analytical store with buffering, backpressure, and at-least-once delivery. Configure partitioning by date/service and a retention tier (hot 90 days, cold archive 1 year).

Deliverables: collector configuration per service, partitioning and retention policy, volume/cost estimate, and a documented onboarding step for a new service.

Acceptance: logs from all in-scope services arrive within the agreed ingest lag; a service emitting a burst of 10x normal volume does not block other services; retention expiry verified on a test partition.

arguments.name: M2.3 Build log parser & pattern extraction
arguments.details:
Parse structured JSON logs directly and plaintext logs via a versioned grok/regex pattern set. Extract fields per M2.1, normalize levels, hash stack traces for grouping, and surface unparsed lines for pattern backfill.

Deliverables: parser configuration with pattern versioning, per-service coverage report, reprocessing path for lines that fail to parse, and unit tests with real sanitized log samples.

Acceptance: >95% of log volume from in-scope services parses successfully; adding a new pattern does not require redeploying the pipeline; a coverage report is queryable.

arguments.name: M2.4 Enrich logs with request, session & customer context
arguments.details:
Join parsed log events with request metadata and pseudonymized customer identifiers so events can be attributed without exposing PII. Apply PII redaction (emails, tokens, card-like patterns) before storage in the analytical layer.

Deliverables: enrichment job, pseudonymization mapping store, redaction rule set, and a PII-in-logs audit report.

Acceptance: sampled log rows contain no raw PII in analytical tables; enrichment hit rate on request id is above target; customers can be traced between log events and the canonical customer model (M1.5) without name/email exposure.

arguments.name: M2.5 Implement sessionization & usage event derivation
arguments.details:
Derive user sessions from log events using an inactivity timeout, and emit normalized usage events (feature viewed, action completed, error encountered) that feed activation/engagement metrics.

Deliverables: session boundary logic, late-arriving-event handling, derived usage event table, and backfill-capable job.

Acceptance: session counts reconcile within tolerance against a manual sample; late events within the allowed window still join the correct session; re-running the job is idempotent.

arguments.name: M2.6 Build operational metric aggregations (error rate, latency, volume)
arguments.details:
Produce hourly and daily aggregates per service/environment: request volume, error rate by category, latency p50/p95/p99, and top error signatures. Store in partitioned aggregate tables sized for fast dashboard reads.

Deliverables: aggregation jobs, aggregate table schemas, backfill job, and a validation query set comparing aggregates to raw-event recomputation.

Acceptance: aggregates match raw recomputation within 0.5%; hourly partitions refresh within the SLA; query latency for a 30-day range stays under the dashboard budget.

arguments.name: M2.7 Implement anomaly detection jobs
arguments.details:
Add baseline-and-deviation detection on the M2.6 aggregates: seasonal/weekly baselines per service, threshold plus statistical deviation scoring, and a materialized anomaly feed consumed by the dashboard.

Deliverables: baseline computation job, detector configuration (sensitivity per metric), anomaly table with score/severity/window, and a tuning note on false-positive rate.

Acceptance: seeded synthetic incidents are detected within one aggregation interval; historical false-positive rate is documented and acceptable to on-call; detectors are configurable without code changes.

arguments.name: M2.8 Wire alert rules & runbook links
arguments.details:
Translate the agreed thresholds and anomaly severities into alert rules with routing, deduplication, and suppression windows. Link every rule to a runbook entry describing first response.

Deliverables: alert rule definitions as code, routing/suppression config, runbook stubs per rule, and an alert test harness (fire a synthetic alert end to end).

Acceptance: each rule fires and resolves correctly in a drill; duplicate alerts within the suppression window collapse to one; no alert exists without a runbook link.

arguments.name: M3.1 Design conformed dimensional model
arguments.details:
Design facts and dimensions that serve both customer and operational dashboards: dim_customer, dim_service, dim_date, dim_error_category, fct_customer_activity, fct_service_health, fct_data_quality.

Deliverables: ERD, grain statement per fact table, conformed dimension definitions, slowly-changing-dimension approach (SCD2 for customer attributes), and a naming convention doc.

Acceptance: design review confirms each dashboard metric can be computed from the model without joins outside the marts; grain is documented and duplicated-grain test cases pass.

arguments.name: M3.2 Build transformation project & data tests
arguments.details:
Implement the M3.1 model as a version-controlled transformation project (staging → intermediate → marts) with built-in tests: unique/not-null keys, referential integrity, accepted values, and row-count/freshness checks.

Deliverables: transformation project repo structure, staging models over M1 and M2 outputs, mart models, test definitions, and generated documentation/lineage graph.

Acceptance: full build runs green from scratch in the dev environment; every fact/dimension has key and referential tests; lineage graph shows no orphan models.

arguments.name: M3.3 Author governed metric definitions catalog
arguments.details:
Write one canonical definition per KPI: business meaning, formula, grain, inclusions/exclusions, time-window semantics, owner, and known caveats. Cover customer metrics (active customers, retention, churn risk, activation) and operational metrics (error rate, availability, p95 latency, incident count).

Deliverables: metric catalog (data-dictionary format, version controlled), glossary of shared business terms, and per-metric owner sign-off.

Acceptance: every dashboard tile maps to exactly one catalog entry; ambiguous pairs (e.g. "active customer" definitions) are resolved and documented; product and engineering both sign off.

arguments.name: M3.4 Implement semantic metric layer
arguments.details:
Encode the M3.3 catalog as a semantic layer (metric definitions, dimensions, joins, time grains) so the same metric cannot be redefined differently per dashboard. Expose metrics by name to consumers.

Deliverables: semantic model files, metric definitions with filters and default time windows, and a metric validation suite comparing layer output to hand-written reference SQL.

Acceptance: all catalog metrics resolve through the semantic layer; reference-SQL comparison matches within tolerance; adding a metric is a config change plus review, not a code fork.

arguments.name: M3.5 Build dashboard query API with caching
arguments.details:
Provide a read API over the semantic layer: metric query endpoint, dimension/filter metadata endpoint, pagination, request timeouts, and a cache keyed by metric + filters + time range with sensible TTLs.

Deliverables: API contract (OpenAPI), cache implementation with invalidation on partition refresh, query cost guardrails (max range, max series), and load-test baseline.

Acceptance: p95 API latency under the agreed budget for standard dashboard ranges; repeated identical queries hit cache; oversized queries are rejected with a clear error rather than timing out.

arguments.name: M3.6 Implement access control & audit logging
arguments.details:
Define roles/personas (executive, analyst, support, engineer), map them to allowed metrics and row scopes (e.g. region or customer segment), and enforce at the query API. Log every query with principal, metrics, filters, and row counts.

Deliverables: role matrix, row-level and column-level policy implementation, audit log table, and access tests per persona.

Acceptance: a persona cannot retrieve data outside its scope (negative tests pass for each role); audit records exist for 100% of queries; PII columns are masked for non-privileged roles.

arguments.name: M4.1 Dashboard UX wireframes & information architecture
arguments.details:
Map the two dashboards tile by tile: which metric, which chart type, which filters, default time ranges, and the primary question each tile answers. Define navigation, layout grid, and empty/loading/error states.

Deliverables: low-fidelity wireframes, tile-to-metric mapping table (linking to M3.3 catalog entries), and a clickable prototype for review.

Acceptance: product stakeholders approve the layout; every tile has a named owner question and a metric id; no tile lacks a data source.

arguments.name: M4.2 Build chart component library foundation
arguments.details:
Set up the component library skeleton: design tokens (color, spacing, typography), theming/light-dark support, a chart wrapper handling sizing/responsiveness, standard axes/legends/tooltips, loading and empty states, and a Storybook workspace.

Deliverables: library package with build config, tokens, base chart wrapper, Storybook setup, and contribution guide.

Acceptance: wrapper renders correctly at mobile/tablet/desktop breakpoints; tokens are the only source of color/spacing values; Storybook builds and publishes.

arguments.name: M4.3 Implement core chart types (timeseries, bar, table, KPI tile)
arguments.details:
Build the four chart types the wireframes require, each accepting the standard chart wrapper's props: line/area timeseries with tooltips, grouped/stacked bar, sortable paginated table with number formatting, and KPI tile with trend/delta indicator and sparkline.

Deliverables: components with typed props, unit tests, Storybook stories per state (populated, empty, loading, error, large dataset), and a data-shape adapter from the M3.5 API response.

Acceptance: each chart handles 1 series and 20 series without layout breakage; number/date formatting matches locale conventions; visual regression snapshots approved.

arguments.name: M4.4 Accessibility & responsive behavior pass on charts
arguments.details:
Make charts usable without a mouse and without color alone: keyboard focus/order, screen-reader summaries and data tables as fallbacks, role/aria attributes, contrast-checked palettes, and responsive reflow rules.

Deliverables: a11y checklist per component, automated axe checks in CI for Storybook stories, screen-reader test notes, and colorblind-safe palette verification.

Acceptance: axe reports zero critical/serious issues on core views; every chart has a text alternative; WCAG 2.1 AA contrast met for text and data series.

arguments.name: M4.5 Assemble customer analytics dashboard
arguments.details:
Compose the customer dashboard from wireframes and library components: active customers, acquisition/cohort retention, churn-risk segmentation, activation funnel, and data-quality health strip. Wire each tile to the M3.5 API by metric id only.

Deliverables: page implementation, per-tile data binding, loading/error/empty handling, and a QA checklist signed off against the wireframes.

Acceptance: all tiles load real data in staging; tile values independently verified against reference SQL for a fixed date range; page renders within the performance budget.

arguments.name: M4.6 Assemble operational & log health dashboard
arguments.details:
Compose the engineering-facing dashboard: error rate and volume timeseries by service, latency percentiles, top error signatures with counts, incident/anomaly feed with severity, and a log parse-coverage indicator.

Deliverables: page implementation, anomaly feed rendering, drill link from anomaly to filtered timeseries, and a QA checklist signed off against wireframes.

Acceptance: dashboards reconcile with M2.6 aggregates; an injected synthetic incident appears in the anomaly feed within one interval; page meets the performance budget.

arguments.name: M4.7 Add global filters, drilldowns & saved views
arguments.details:
Implement the shared filter bar (date range, segment, region, service, environment), URL-encoded state so views are linkable, drilldown from chart point to filtered detail, and save/name/share a view.

Deliverables: filter state manager, URL serialization, drilldown interactions, saved-view storage, and tests for state restoration.

Acceptance: a shared link reproduces the exact filters and time range for another user; drilldown preserves parent filters; saved views respect the viewer's access scope rather than the creator's.

arguments.name: M4.8 Implement export & sharing
arguments.details:
Add CSV export of the underlying tile data, PNG/image export of a chart, and scheduled email/slack digest of a dashboard snapshot. Exports must respect the same access controls as the UI and be audit-logged.

Deliverables: export service/endpoints, scheduled digest job, rate limiting, and an audit trail for exports.

Acceptance: exported CSV matches on-screen values exactly; a user cannot export data outside their scope; scheduled digest delivers to a test channel on time.

arguments.name: M5.1 Provision environments with infrastructure as code
arguments.details:
Define dev, staging, and prod environments declaratively: storage, warehouse, compute for pipelines, API hosting, frontend hosting, secrets management, and network/egress rules.

Deliverables: IaC modules per environment, parameterized config, secrets handling policy, and a documented promote-to-prod path.

Acceptance: a clean environment can be created from code with one command and torn down cleanly; no secrets in the repo; staging is a functional mirror of prod configuration.

arguments.name: M5.2 Set up CI/CD pipelines with quality gates
arguments.details:
Build pipelines for the transformation project, API, and frontend: lint, unit tests, data tests on a sample dataset, build, and staged deploy. Add quality gates that block merges on failure.

Deliverables: pipeline definitions, branch protection + required checks, artifact versioning, and a rollback job.

Acceptance: a failing data test blocks deployment; a green change reaches staging automatically and prod on approval; median pipeline duration is under the agreed limit.

arguments.name: M5.3 Instrument observability & define data SLAs
arguments.details:
Add metrics, logs, and traces for the platform itself (pipeline run outcomes, durations, lag, API error/latency, cache hit rate) and publish data SLAs: freshness, completeness, and availability targets per dataset.

Deliverables: dashboards for platform health, alert rules tied to SLA breaches, and a published SLA doc with owners and escalation.

Acceptance: a deliberately failed pipeline run raises an alert within the target window; freshness and completeness are visible per dataset; SLA doc approved by stakeholders.

arguments.name: M5.4 Build integration & data-contract test suite
arguments.details:
Beyond unit tests, add end-to-end tests: fixture CSV through the full ingestion path, synthetic logs through parsing to aggregates, contract tests that fail if a source schema changes incompatibly, and API contract tests against the frontend.

Deliverables: integration test harness with seeded fixtures, schema-drift contract tests, API contract tests, and a coverage report.

Acceptance: the suite catches an intentionally introduced schema change and an intentionally broken metric; tests run in CI in under the agreed duration; coverage of critical paths documented.

arguments.name: M5.5 Run performance & load testing
arguments.details:
Load-test the query API and dashboard pages at expected and 3x expected concurrency, and benchmark pipeline throughput on production-sized files and log volumes.

Deliverables: load-test scripts and scenarios, baseline results, bottleneck list with fixes, and documented capacity headroom.

Acceptance: p95 dashboard API latency stays within budget at 3x expected concurrency; a production-sized CSV completes ingestion inside its window; identified bottlenecks are fixed or explicitly accepted with a follow-up task.

arguments.name: M5.6 Security review, PII handling & compliance sign-off
arguments.details:
Review the end-to-end data flow for PII exposure, verify redaction in logs and masking in dashboards/exports, check secrets handling, dependency and image scanning, access reviews, and retention/deletion obligations.

Deliverables: threat-model summary, findings log with severity and remediation status, data retention/deletion policy, and signed compliance sign-off.

Acceptance: no high/critical findings open at launch; PII audit passes on analytical tables; deletion request path verified end to end.

arguments.name: M5.7 Write runbooks, docs & enablement materials
arguments.details:
Produce operator and user documentation: architecture overview, on-call runbooks for each alert, metric glossary (from M3.3), onboarding for new data sources and new services, FAQ for dashboard users, and a short training walkthrough.

Deliverables: docs site or repo section, runbooks linked from alerts, onboarding checklists, and a recorded enablement session.

Acceptance: a new engineer can run the pipeline and resolve a sample failed run using only the docs; support team completes training and answers a sample user question set.

arguments.name: M5.8 Execute phased rollout & rollback rehearsal
arguments.details:
Roll out in phases: internal pilot, one business unit, then general availability. Define entry/exit criteria per phase, feedback capture, and rehearse rollback of both dashboard and pipeline.

Deliverables: rollout plan with phase gates, pilot feedback log, rollback rehearsal record with timings, and a launch checklist.

Acceptance: pilot exit criteria met before expansion; rollback rehearsal completes inside the target recovery window; launch checklist fully signed.

Acceptance: every rejected row is explainable from the quarantine record; fix-and-reprocess moves a row out of quarantine correctly; DQ metrics queryable with <5s latency.

tasks.name: M1.7 Add incremental load & backfill orchestration
tasks.details:
Wrap the ingestion pieces (intake → parse → validate → dedupe → normalize) in an orchestrated, scheduled workflow with retries, alerting on failure, and a parameterized backfill mode for historical files.

Deliverables: orchestration DAG/job definitions, watermark/checkpoint logic for incremental runs, backfill runbook, retry and dead-letter behavior.

Acceptance: scheduled run processes only new files; a 12-month backfill completes within the window and is safely resumable after interruption; failed runs raise an alert and can be re-run without duplication.

tasks.name: M2.1 Define log event schema & field taxonomy
tasks.details:
Agree the canonical log event: timestamp (UTC), service, environment, level, logger, message, trace/request id, user/customer id, latency, status code, error type/stack hash, plus a taxonomy of event names and error categories used by the dashboard.

Deliverables: schema doc, enum values for level/error category, guidance for app teams on emitting structured JSON logs, and a backward-compatibility note for existing plaintext formats.

Acceptance: schema approved by the app engineering leads; every field the dashboard needs is sourced from this schema (no ad hoc parsing in the UI).

tasks.name: M2.2 Collect application logs into central store
tasks.details:
Wire application log shipping into the central analytical store with buffering, backpressure, and at-least-once delivery. Configure partitioning by date/service and a retention tier (hot 90 days, cold archive 1 year).

Deliverables: collector configuration per service, partitioning and retention policy, volume/cost estimate, and a documented onboarding step for a new service.

Acceptance: logs from all in-scope services arrive within the agreed ingest lag; a service emitting a burst of 10x normal volume does not block other services; retention expiry verified on a test partition.

tasks.name: M2.3 Build log parser & pattern extraction
tasks.details:
Parse structured JSON logs directly and plaintext logs via a versioned grok/regex pattern set. Extract fields per M2.1, normalize levels, hash stack traces for grouping, and surface unparsed lines for pattern backfill.

Deliverables: parser configuration with pattern versioning, per-service coverage report, reprocessing path for lines that fail to parse, and unit tests with real sanitized log samples.

Acceptance: >95% of log volume from in-scope services parses successfully; adding a new pattern does not require redeploying the pipeline; a coverage report is queryable.

tasks.name: M2.4 Enrich logs with request, session & customer context
tasks.details:
Join parsed log events with request metadata and pseudonymized customer identifiers so events can be attributed without exposing PII. Apply PII redaction (emails, tokens, card-like patterns) before storage in the analytical layer.

Deliverables: enrichment job, pseudonymization mapping store, redaction rule set, and a PII-in-logs audit report.

Acceptance: sampled log rows contain no raw PII in analytical tables; enrichment hit rate on request id is above target; customers can be traced between log events and the canonical customer model (M1.5) without name/email exposure.

tasks.name: M2.5 Implement sessionization & usage event derivation
tasks.details:
Derive user sessions from log events using an inactivity timeout, and emit normalized usage events (feature viewed, action completed, error encountered) that feed activation/engagement metrics.

Deliverables: session boundary logic, late-arriving-event handling, derived usage event table, and backfill-capable job.

Acceptance: session counts reconcile within tolerance against a manual sample; late events within the allowed window still join the correct session; re-running the job is idempotent.

tasks.name: M2.6 Build operational metric aggregations (error rate, latency, volume)
tasks.details:
Produce hourly and daily aggregates per service/environment: request volume, error rate by category, latency p50/p95/p99, and top error signatures. Store in partitioned aggregate tables sized for fast dashboard reads.

Deliverables: aggregation jobs, aggregate table schemas, backfill job, and a validation query set comparing aggregates to raw-event recomputation.

Acceptance: aggregates match raw recomputation within 0.5%; hourly partitions refresh within the SLA; query latency for a 30-day range stays under the dashboard budget.

tasks.name: M2.7 Implement anomaly detection jobs
tasks.details:
Add baseline-and-deviation detection on the M2.6 aggregates: seasonal/weekly baselines per service, threshold plus statistical deviation scoring, and a materialized anomaly feed consumed by the dashboard.

Deliverables: baseline computation job, detector configuration (sensitivity per metric), anomaly table with score/severity/window, and a tuning note on false-positive rate.

Acceptance: seeded synthetic incidents are detected within one aggregation interval; historical false-positive rate is documented and acceptable to on-call; detectors are configurable without code changes.

tasks.name: M2.8 Wire alert rules & runbook links
tasks.details:
Translate the agreed thresholds and anomaly severities into alert rules with routing, deduplication, and suppression windows. Link every rule to a runbook entry describing first response.

Deliverables: alert rule definitions as code, routing/suppression config, runbook stubs per rule, and an alert test harness (fire a synthetic alert end to end).

Acceptance: each rule fires and resolves correctly in a drill; duplicate alerts within the suppression window collapse to one; no alert exists without a runbook link.

tasks.name: M3.1 Design conformed dimensional model
tasks.details:
Design facts and dimensions that serve both customer and operational dashboards: dim_customer, dim_service, dim_date, dim_error_category, fct_customer_activity, fct_service_health, fct_data_quality.

Deliverables: ERD, grain statement per fact table, conformed dimension definitions, slowly-changing-dimension approach (SCD2 for customer attributes), and a naming convention doc.

Acceptance: design review confirms each dashboard metric can be computed from the model without joins outside the marts; grain is documented and duplicated-grain test cases pass.

tasks.name: M3.2 Build transformation project & data tests
tasks.details:
Implement the M3.1 model as a version-controlled transformation project (staging → intermediate → marts) with built-in tests: unique/not-null keys, referential integrity, accepted values, and row-count/freshness checks.

Deliverables: transformation project repo structure, staging models over M1 and M2 outputs, mart models, test definitions, and generated documentation/lineage graph.

Acceptance: full build runs green from scratch in the dev environment; every fact/dimension has key and referential tests; lineage graph shows no orphan models.

tasks.name: M3.3 Author governed metric definitions catalog
tasks.details:
Write one canonical definition per KPI: business meaning, formula, grain, inclusions/exclusions, time-window semantics, owner, and known caveats. Cover customer metrics (active customers, retention, churn risk, activation) and operational metrics (error rate, availability, p95 latency, incident count).

Deliverables: metric catalog (data-dictionary format, version controlled), glossary of shared business terms, and per-metric owner sign-off.

Acceptance: every dashboard tile maps to exactly one catalog entry; ambiguous pairs (e.g. "active customer" definitions) are resolved and documented; product and engineering both sign off.

tasks.name: M3.4 Implement semantic metric layer
tasks.details:
Encode the M3.3 catalog as a semantic layer (metric definitions, dimensions, joins, time grains) so the same metric cannot be redefined differently per dashboard. Expose metrics by name to consumers.

Deliverables: semantic model files, metric definitions with filters and default time windows, and a metric validation suite comparing layer output to hand-written reference SQL.

Acceptance: all catalog metrics resolve through the semantic layer; reference-SQL comparison matches within tolerance; adding a metric is a config change plus review, not a code fork.

tasks.name: M3.5 Build dashboard query API with caching
tasks.details:
Provide a read API over the semantic layer: metric query endpoint, dimension/filter metadata endpoint, pagination, request timeouts, and a cache keyed by metric + filters + time range with sensible TTLs.

Deliverables: API contract (OpenAPI), cache implementation with invalidation on partition refresh, query cost guardrails (max range, max series), and load-test baseline.

Acceptance: p95 API latency under the agreed budget for standard dashboard ranges; repeated identical queries hit cache; oversized queries are rejected with a clear error rather than timing out.

tasks.name: M3.6 Implement access control & audit logging
tasks.details:
Define roles/personas (executive, analyst, support, engineer), map them to allowed metrics and row scopes (e.g. region or customer segment), and enforce at the query API. Log every query with principal, metrics, filters, and row counts.

Deliverables: role matrix, row-level and column-level policy implementation, audit log table, and access tests per persona.

Acceptance: a persona cannot retrieve data outside its scope (negative tests pass for each role); audit records exist for 100% of queries; PII columns are masked for non-privileged roles.

tasks.name: M4.1 Dashboard UX wireframes & information architecture
tasks.details:
Map the two dashboards tile by tile: which metric, which chart type, which filters, default time ranges, and the primary question each tile answers. Define navigation, layout grid, and empty/loading/error states.

Deliverables: low-fidelity wireframes, tile-to-metric mapping table (linking to M3.3 catalog entries), and a clickable prototype for review.

Acceptance: product stakeholders approve the layout; every tile has a named owner question and a metric id; no tile lacks a data source.

tasks.name: M4.2 Build chart component library foundation
tasks.details:
Set up the component library skeleton: design tokens (color, spacing, typography), theming/light-dark support, a chart wrapper handling sizing/responsiveness, standard axes/legends/tooltips, loading and empty states, and a Storybook workspace.

Deliverables: library package with build config, tokens, base chart wrapper, Storybook setup, and contribution guide.

Acceptance: wrapper renders correctly at mobile/tablet/desktop breakpoints; tokens are the only source of color/spacing values; Storybook builds and publishes.

tasks.name: M4.3 Implement core chart types (timeseries, bar, table, KPI tile)
tasks.details:
Build the four chart types the wireframes require, each accepting the standard chart wrapper's props: line/area timeseries with tooltips, grouped/stacked bar, sortable paginated table with number formatting, and KPI tile with trend/delta indicator and sparkline.

Deliverables: components with typed props, unit tests, Storybook stories per state (populated, empty, loading, error, large dataset), and a data-shape adapter from the M3.5 API response.

Acceptance: each chart handles 1 series and 20 series without layout breakage; number/date formatting matches locale conventions; visual regression snapshots approved.

tasks.name: M4.4 Accessibility & responsive behavior pass on charts
tasks.details:
Make charts usable without a mouse and without color alone: keyboard focus/order, screen-reader summaries and data tables as fallbacks, role/aria attributes, contrast-checked palettes, and responsive reflow rules.

Deliverables: a11y checklist per component, automated axe checks in CI for Storybook stories, screen-reader test notes, and colorblind-safe palette verification.

Acceptance: axe reports zero critical/serious issues on core views; every chart has a text alternative; WCAG 2.1 AA contrast met for text and data series.

tasks.name: M4.5 Assemble customer analytics dashboard
tasks.details:
Compose the customer dashboard from wireframes and library components: active customers, acquisition/cohort retention, churn-risk segmentation, activation funnel, and data-quality health strip. Wire each tile to the M3.5 API by metric id only.

Deliverables: page implementation, per-tile data binding, loading/error/empty handling, and a QA checklist signed off against the wireframes.

Acceptance: all tiles load real data in staging; tile values independently verified against reference SQL for a fixed date range; page renders within the performance budget.

tasks.name: M4.6 Assemble operational & log health dashboard
tasks.details:
Compose the engineering-facing dashboard: error rate and volume timeseries by service, latency percentiles, top error signatures with counts, incident/anomaly feed with severity, and a log parse-coverage indicator.

Deliverables: page implementation, anomaly feed rendering, drill link from anomaly to filtered timeseries, and a QA checklist signed off against wireframes.

Acceptance: dashboards reconcile with M2.6 aggregates; an injected synthetic incident appears in the anomaly feed within one interval; page meets the performance budget.

tasks.name: M4.7 Add global filters, drilldowns & saved views
tasks.details:
Implement the shared filter bar (date range, segment, region, service, environment), URL-encoded state so views are linkable, drilldown from chart point to filtered detail, and save/name/share a view.

Deliverables: filter state manager, URL serialization, drilldown interactions, saved-view storage, and tests for state restoration.

Acceptance: a shared link reproduces the exact filters and time range for another user; drilldown preserves parent filters; saved views respect the viewer's access scope rather than the creator's.

tasks.name: M4.8 Implement export & sharing
tasks.details:
Add CSV export of the underlying tile data, PNG/image export of a chart, and scheduled email/slack digest of a dashboard snapshot. Exports must respect the same access controls as the UI and be audit-logged.

Deliverables: export service/endpoints, scheduled digest job, rate limiting, and an audit trail for exports.

Acceptance: exported CSV matches on-screen values exactly; a user cannot export data outside their scope; scheduled digest delivers to a test channel on time.

tasks.name: M5.1 Provision environments with infrastructure as code
tasks.details:
Define dev, staging, and prod environments declaratively: storage, warehouse, compute for pipelines, API hosting, frontend hosting, secrets management, and network/egress rules.

Deliverables: IaC modules per environment, parameterized config, secrets handling policy, and a documented promote-to-prod path.

Acceptance: a clean environment can be created from code with one command and torn down cleanly; no secrets in the repo; staging is a functional mirror of prod configuration.

tasks.name: M5.2 Set up CI/CD pipelines with quality gates
tasks.details:
Build pipelines for the transformation project, API, and frontend: lint, unit tests, data tests on a sample dataset, build, and staged deploy. Add quality gates that block merges on failure.

Deliverables: pipeline definitions, branch protection + required checks, artifact versioning, and a rollback job.

Acceptance: a failing data test blocks deployment; a green change reaches staging automatically and prod on approval; median pipeline duration is under the agreed limit.

tasks.name: M5.3 Instrument observability & define data SLAs
tasks.details:
Add metrics, logs, and traces for the platform itself (pipeline run outcomes, durations, lag, API error/latency, cache hit rate) and publish data SLAs: freshness, completeness, and availability targets per dataset.

Deliverables: dashboards for platform health, alert rules tied to SLA breaches, and a published SLA doc with owners and escalation.

Acceptance: a deliberately failed pipeline run raises an alert within the target window; freshness and completeness are visible per dataset; SLA doc approved by stakeholders.

tasks.name: M5.4 Build integration & data-contract test suite
tasks.details:
Beyond unit tests, add end-to-end tests: fixture CSV through the full ingestion path, synthetic logs through parsing to aggregates, contract tests that fail if a source schema changes incompatibly, and API contract tests against the frontend.

Deliverables: integration test harness with seeded fixtures, schema-drift contract tests, API contract tests, and a coverage report.

Acceptance: the suite catches an intentionally introduced schema change and an intentionally broken metric; tests run in CI in under the agreed duration; coverage of critical paths documented.

tasks.name: M5.5 Run performance & load testing
tasks.details:
Load-test the query API and dashboard pages at expected and 3x expected concurrency, and benchmark pipeline throughput on production-sized files and log volumes.

Deliverables: load-test scripts and scenarios, baseline results, bottleneck list with fixes, and documented capacity headroom.

Acceptance: p95 dashboard API latency stays within budget at 3x expected concurrency; a production-sized CSV completes ingestion inside its window; identified bottlenecks are fixed or explicitly accepted with a follow-up task.

tasks.name: M5.6 Security review, PII handling & compliance sign-off
tasks.details:
Review the end-to-end data flow for PII exposure, verify redaction in logs and masking in dashboards/exports, check secrets handling, dependency and image scanning, access reviews, and retention/deletion obligations.

Deliverables: threat-model summary, findings log with severity and remediation status, data retention/deletion policy, and signed compliance sign-off.

Acceptance: no high/critical findings open at launch; PII audit passes on analytical tables; deletion request path verified end to end.

tasks.name: M5.7 Write runbooks, docs & enablement materials
tasks.details:
Produce operator and user documentation: architecture overview, on-call runbooks for each alert, metric glossary (from M3.3), onboarding for new data sources and new services, FAQ for dashboard users, and a short training walkthrough.

Deliverables: docs site or repo section, runbooks linked from alerts, onboarding checklists, and a recorded enablement session.

Acceptance: a new engineer can run the pipeline and resolve a sample failed run using only the docs; support team completes training and answers a sample user question set.

tasks.name: M5.8 Execute phased rollout & rollback rehearsal
tasks.details:
Roll out in phases: internal pilot, one business unit, then general availability. Define entry/exit criteria per phase, feedback capture, and rehearse rollback of both dashboard and pipeline.

Deliverables: rollout plan with phase gates, pilot feedback log, rollback rehearsal record with timings, and a launch checklist.

Acceptance: pilot exit criteria met before expansion; rollback rehearsal completes inside the target recovery window; launch checklist fully signed.

arguments.name: Analytics Dashboard Platform
arguments.description:
Build an analytics dashboard platform that ingests and processes customer CSV files, analyzes application logs, and presents insights through interactive visualization components.

Scope:
- CSV ingestion pipeline for customer data (schema validation, normalization, incremental loads)
- Application log analysis (parsing, correlation IDs, error/severity aggregation, time-series metrics)
- Unified data model / metrics layer serving both sources
- Reusable visualization component library and dashboard composition
- Testing, performance, deployment and operational readiness

Delivery approach: milestone-based, with every task sized for a single owner to complete in under ~2 days of work; anything larger is decomposed into subtasks.

arguments.name: M1 — Foundation & Architecture
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Agree on what we are measuring, settle the architecture, and have a working repo + environments so pipeline work can start immediately.

Exit criteria:
- KPI/metrics catalog signed off by stakeholders
- Architecture + data flow diagram reviewed
- Repo, CI pipeline, and dev/staging environments provisioned
- Data contracts for customer CSV and log events published

arguments.name: M2 — Customer CSV Ingestion & Processing
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Reliably ingest customer CSV files of varying quality and produce a clean, deduplicated, incrementally-updatable customer dataset.

Exit criteria:
- Any vendor CSV variant in the documented contract can be ingested without manual edits
- Malformed rows are quarantined with actionable error reports, never silently dropped
- Backfills and incremental loads are idempotent and re-runnable
- Data quality checks run automatically and alert on anomalies

arguments.name: M3 — Application Log Analysis
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Turn raw application logs into trustworthy operational metrics (error rates, latency percentiles, throughput, top failure signatures) while handling PII and volume responsibly.

Exit criteria:
- All in-scope log formats parse with a measured success rate
- Events are correlatable across a request/session via correlation IDs
- Aggregation jobs produce hourly/daily metrics that reconcile with raw counts
- PII redaction and retention policies enforced in code, not convention

arguments.name: M4 — Unified Data Model & Metrics Layer
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Give both data sources a common storage layout, shared dimensions, and a single query service the frontend can depend on.

Exit criteria:
- Customer and log facts land in a partitioned, documented warehouse schema
- Shared conformed dimensions (date, customer, service, environment) exist once, not per-source
- Metrics query API serves dashboard needs with p95 latency inside target
- Caching strategy documented with invalidation rules

arguments.name: M5 — Visualization Component Library
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Build the reusable, themed, accessible chart and control primitives the dashboard pages will compose — one implementation each, not bespoke charts per page.

Exit criteria:
- Chart primitives (line, bar, area, donut) share one data interface and theming source
- Table, filter, and KPI tile components handle loading/empty/error states
- Component Storybook (or equivalent) covers every component with examples
- Accessibility checks pass for keyboard nav, contrast, and screen-reader labels

arguments.name: M6 — Dashboard Composition & UX
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Assemble the components into the two real product surfaces — customer analytics and operations/log health — with working filters, drill-downs, and export.

Exit criteria:
- Customer analytics page and operations page both complete against the metrics catalog
- Global filters (date range, customer segment, service, environment) drive every panel
- Click-through from a chart to underlying records works end to end
- Export and share links produce reproducible views

arguments.name: M7 — Testing, Performance & Security
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Prove the pipelines and dashboards are correct, fast enough, and safe to expose to users.

Exit criteria:
- Automated test coverage on transforms and API contracts at agreed thresholds
- Load test results at 2x expected peak volume documented
- PII/access-control review completed with findings remediated or accepted
- No open Sev-1/Sev-2 defects at milestone close

arguments.name: M8 — Deployment, Operations & Rollout
arguments.details:
MILESTONE CONTAINER (progress tracked via child tasks).

Goal: Ship to production with infrastructure as code, alerting on the things that actually break, runbooks, and a feedback loop with real users.

Exit criteria:
- Production infrastructure reproducible from code, one-command deploy
- Pipeline SLIs/alerts live (freshness, failure rate, quarantine volume)
- Runbooks exist for the top five failure scenarios and were dry-run once
- Beta cohort onboarded with a tracked feedback backlog

arguments.name: Define metrics catalog and KPI definitions
arguments.details:
Deliverable: A single metrics catalog document (or YAML file in the repo) that every downstream task builds against.

Contents — one entry per metric, with:
- Name, plain-English definition, and the exact formula
- Source (customer CSV / app logs / derived) and grain (per-customer, per-hour, per-request)
- Dimensions it can be sliced by (date, segment, service, environment)
- Known caveats (late-arriving data, duplicate rows, timezone assumptions)
- Owner / stakeholder who signs off

Cover at minimum: active customers, new vs. churned customers, revenue per segment, error rate, p95/p99 latency, request throughput, top error signatures.

Done when: reviewed with stakeholders, all open questions resolved or explicitly deferred, catalog committed to the repo.

Sized to fit in one day; do not expand into dashboard design here.

arguments.name: Set up repository, CI pipeline, and dev/staging environments
arguments.details:
Deliverable: A working skeleton everyone can pull and deploy from on day one.

Steps:
- Create the monorepo with folders for ingestion, transforms, api, frontend, infra, docs
- Add linting/formatting, pre-commit hooks, and a standard PR template
- Configure CI to run lint + unit tests + build on every PR
- Provision dev and staging environments (containerized locally, managed in staging)
- Add secret management and .env.example conventions; no credentials in the repo
- Write a 1-page CONTRIBUTING / local-setup guide

Done when: a new developer clones the repo and runs the stack locally by following the README, and CI is green on an empty PR.

Deliberately excludes production infrastructure (see M8).

arguments.name: Design platform architecture and data flow
arguments.details:
Deliverable: One architecture decision record (ADR) plus a data-flow diagram committed under /docs.

Cover, with a decision and a one-line rationale for each:

- Storage choice: warehouse tables + object storage for raw files; partitioning strategy

Current implementation relies on eval()/exec() on raw request strings, sometimes with dynamic imports and attribute access enabled.
arguments.framework: Flask / FastAPI with untrusted expression input
securityRequirements: No use of eval/exec/compile on untrusted input; replace with a parser-AST evaluator using ast.parse(mode='eval') and an explicit node allowlist
Reject names, attribute access, subscripts, lambdas, comprehensions, and dunder identifiers during AST walks
Enforce hard limits: expression length, AST node count, nesting depth, exponents, and integer digit size to prevent DoS
Bound function calls to a strict allowlisted math namespace with callable, arity, and numeric-type checks
Validate and normalize numeric types (int/float/Decimal) with NaN/Infinity rejection
Handle errors without leaking stack traces, source or internals; log with correlation IDs
Add rate limiting, request size limits, and per-request execution timeouts/circuit breakers
Keep the parser/evaluator and its dependencies patched; pin versions and scan for CVEs
Add adversarial unit tests (OWASP-style payload corpus) into CI as a security gate

Then create an area chart showing monthly sales trends from January to December 2025, with values: Jan: 1.2M, Feb: 1.1M, Mar: 1.4M, Apr: 1.6M, May: 1.8M, Jun: 2.1M, Jul: 2.3M, Aug: 2.2M, Sep: 2.5M, Oct: 2.7M, Nov: 3.0M, Dec: 3.5M. Finally, make a column chart comparing our top product categories across regions: Electronics (Guangdong: 6.2M, Jiangsu: 4.8M), Home Appliances (Guangdong: 4.5M, Jiangsu: 3.9M), and Clothing (Guangdong: 5.1M, Jiangsu: 3.6M).

- 江苏省 (Jiangsu): ¥12.3M
- 浙江省 (Zhejiang): ¥9.7M
- 山东省 (Shandong): ¥8.4M

**2. Monthly Sales Trend Area Chart (2025年月度销售额趋势)**

- Steady acceleration from spring onward (Jun 2.1M, Sep 2.5M)

arguments.name: Customer Analytics Dashboard
arguments.description:
Analytics dashboard platform combining three data streams: (1) batch processing of customer CSV files, (2) analysis of application log data, and (3) a visualization layer of charts and dashboards. Scope covers ingestion and transformation, log parsing and metrics, the dashboard UI, and the shared platform work needed to run it in production.

Structure: four milestone-level epics, each decomposed into executable tasks sized at complexity <= 5 so that every task is independently actionable by a single contributor.

arguments.name: M1: Customer CSV Data Pipeline
arguments.details:
Milestone / epic container. Deliver a repeatable pipeline that ingests customer CSV exports, validates and normalizes them, and produces analytics-ready customer tables.

Exit criteria: any new customer CSV drop is validated, transformed, and queryable within the agreed SLA with no manual steps; rejected rows are quarantined with reasons.

NOTE: This epic is intentionally not executable as a single work item - it is fully decomposed into subtasks of complexity <= 5.

arguments.name: M2: Application Log Analysis
arguments.details:
Milestone / epic container. Turn raw application log output into reliable, queryable operational metrics (error rates, latency, request volume) and surface anomalies worth alerting on.

Exit criteria: log metrics are produced on a schedule, match source logs within tolerance, and at least one anomaly/alert rule is validated against historical data.

NOTE: This epic is intentionally not executable as a single work item - it is fully decomposed into subtasks of complexity <= 5.

arguments.name: M3: Visualization & Dashboard UI
arguments.details:
Milestone / epic container. Build the dashboard experience: a reusable chart component set, composed dashboard pages for customer and operational metrics, and the filter/drill-down behavior analysts expect.

Exit criteria: a stakeholder-approved dashboard loads in under the agreed latency budget, is keyboard accessible, and every chart traces to a defined metric in the catalog.

NOTE: This epic is intentionally not executable as a single work item - it is fully decomposed into subtasks of complexity <= 5.

arguments.name: M4: Platform Foundations & Production Launch
arguments.details:
Milestone / epic container. Everything the three feature streams depend on to run as one product: data model and storage decisions, orchestration and scheduling, access control, end-to-end verification, and launch readiness.

Exit criteria: pipeline, log analytics, and dashboards run together in a staging environment; access is role-gated; runbook and ownership are documented; go/no-go review signed off.

NOTE: This epic is intentionally not executable as a single work item - it is fully decomposed into subtasks of complexity <= 5.

arguments.name: Profile customer CSV sources and document the schema contract
arguments.details:
Inventory every customer CSV export we receive (or expect to receive). For 3-5 representative files record: column names, inferred types, null rates, cardinality, encoding, delimiter, row counts, and known quirks (free-text fields, mixed date formats, currency symbols).

Output: a schema contract document listing required vs optional columns, accepted formats, and the field-level validation rules downstream tasks will implement. Confirm priorities and edge cases with the business owner of the customer data.

Done when: the contract is reviewed and signed off, and at least one sample file per source is stored as a test fixture.

arguments.name: Build the CSV ingestion loader
arguments.details:
Implement the component that discovers and reads customer CSV drop files and lands them in raw storage.

In scope: file discovery/trigger, streaming read so 1GB+ files do not exhaust memory, encoding and delimiter detection, header mapping to the schema contract, and idempotent naming in the landing zone. Out of scope: validation logic and business transformations (separate tasks).

Done when: the loader runs end-to-end on the fixtures from the profiling task and a re-run of the same file does not create duplicates.

arguments.name: Implement row validation and bad-row quarantine
arguments.details:
Apply the field-level rules from the schema contract: required fields, type/date parsing, enum and range checks, referential sanity (e.g. customer id format), and duplicate key detection within a file.

Rows that fail must be written to a quarantine table with the source file, row number, failing rule, and raw value, while valid rows continue through. Distinguish fatal file-level errors (wrong header, unreadable encoding) from row-level rejects.

Done when: a deliberately corrupted fixture produces the expected split of accepted vs quarantined rows and every reject has a readable reason.

arguments.name: Transform validated rows into the analytics customer model
arguments.details:
Map validated raw rows onto the analytics customer table agreed in the data model task: type casting, date normalization to UTC, trimming/casing of text, currency and country code standardization, and derived attributes (e.g. tenure band, active flag).

Keep the mapping declarative and versioned so a schema change is a config edit rather than a code rewrite. Document each derived field's definition.

Done when: transformations are covered by unit tests on fixtures and the output matches the agreed model with no unmapped columns.

arguments.name: Handle deduplication, identity matching and re-delivered files
arguments.details:
Customers arrive in multiple overlapping exports, so define and implement: the business key for a customer record, which fields win on conflict (most recent snapshot vs most complete record), and how soft-deletes are represented.

Implement upsert/merge behavior so a corrected or re-delivered file updates existing records instead of duplicating them, plus a change-detection check to skip unchanged files.

Done when: replaying the same file twice, and loading a newer snapshot of an existing customer, both leave exactly one row per customer with the expected field values.

arguments.name: Add pipeline data-quality checks and failure reporting
arguments.details:
Wrap the pipeline in post-load assertions: row-count variance versus the previous run, null-rate ceilings on critical fields, referential integrity to the customer dimension, and a freshness check.

On failure or threshold breach, emit a structured run summary (files processed, rows accepted/quarantined, checks passed/failed) and route it to the alerting channel chosen in the platform milestone.

Done when: a seeded regression (e.g. 40% row drop) trips a check and produces an actionable notification.

arguments.name: Inventory application log sources and formats
arguments.details:
Catalogue where logs live today: services producing them, transport (file, stdout, agent, log service), retention, daily volume, and current format (plaintext, JSON lines, mixed).

Sample each source and record the fields available: timestamp, level, service, request id, status code, latency, user/customer id, message, stack traces. Note which fields are missing or inconsistent - these drive the parsing task and any app-side logging changes.

Done when: a one-page inventory exists listing each source, its volume, format and field coverage, plus a list of logging gaps the team accepts for v1.

arguments.name: Parse and normalize logs into structured events
arguments.details:
Build the parsing stage that converts each source's log lines into one normalized event schema: timestamp (UTC), level, service, environment, request id, status code, latency ms, customer id when present, plus the raw message for fallback search.

Handle multi-line stack traces by grouping them with their parent event, and count (do not silently drop) unparseable lines so the malformed-log rate is visible.

Done when: a fixture set per source parses at the agreed success rate and the unparsed remainder is logged with samples for follow-up.

arguments.name: Write metric definitions for log-based KPIs
arguments.details:
Define each metric the dashboard will show from logs, in the same catalog format the visualization milestone uses. For every metric state: precise formula, source fields, inclusion/exclusion rules (health checks, bots, internal calls), aggregation window, unit, and known blind spots.

Initial set: request volume, error rate (5xx and 4xx separately), p50/p95/p99 latency, top error signatures, and per-endpoint availability.

Done when: definitions are reviewed by the dashboard consumers and each one is unambiguous enough for an independent engineer to implement without asking questions.

arguments.name: Compute error-rate, latency and volume aggregates
arguments.details:
Implement the aggregation job that reads normalized events for a time window and writes rollups at the granularities the dashboard needs (e.g. 1-minute for recent, hourly for trends), sliced by service, endpoint and environment.

Requirements: windowed/streaming aggregation over bounded memory, late-arriving event handling, and backfill support for arbitrary historical ranges.

Done when: one week of historical logs is rolled up and the job can re-run a given window idempotently.

arguments.name: Add log anomaly detection and alert rules
arguments.details:
Start with simple, explainable rules rather than a model: static thresholds on error rate and p95 latency, plus a rolling-baseline deviation (e.g. error rate above N standard deviations of the same hour last week).

Include error-signature grouping (normalize ids/numbers out of messages) so one new exception type becomes one alert, plus deduplication and a cooldown to avoid alert storms.

Done when: rules run against two weeks of history, produce a tolerable false-positive rate, and a simulated incident fires exactly one alert.

arguments.name: Reconcile log metrics against source logs
arguments.details:
Validate that aggregates are trustworthy before they are shown to stakeholders. For three sample windows, independently count requests and errors straight from the raw logs and compare with the pipeline's output; investigate and document every discrepancy above 0.5%.

Also verify timestamp/timezone handling and that nothing is double-counted at window boundaries.

Done when: a short reconciliation note records the compared windows, the deltas, and the accepted tolerance.

arguments.name: Define metric catalog and dashboard wireframes
arguments.details:
Agree on one shared metric catalog (name, definition, owner, source, refresh cadence) covering both customer and log metrics, then sketch the dashboard pages as low-fidelity wireframes.

Decide the primary questions each page answers, the 3-5 headline KPIs on top, and the supporting charts beneath. Get explicit sign-off from the main stakeholder so the build tasks have a fixed target.

Done when: catalog and wireframes are approved and stored in the repo, and each visual maps to exactly one catalog metric.

arguments.name: Scaffold the dashboard app with routing and design tokens
arguments.details:
Stand up the frontend application shell: build tooling, TypeScript config, lint/format, page routing for the customer and operations dashboards, and a design-token layer (color, spacing, typography, chart palette).

Keep it deliberately thin - layout primitives and a page shell only. Charting and data fetching are separate tasks.

Done when: the app runs locally, renders both empty dashboard routes, and passes lint plus a production build.

arguments.name: Build the reusable chart component library
arguments.details:
Implement the small set of visuals the wireframes actually need: line/area trend, bar, stacked bar, data table, KPI tile with delta, and sparkline. Each component takes a typed props contract and handles empty, loading and partial-data states.

Build on an existing charting library rather than hand-rolling scales and axes. Wrap it so the rest of the app never imports the library directly.

Done when: a component gallery page renders every chart with fixture data, and each is covered by a render test.

arguments.name: Wire the dashboard data-fetching layer
arguments.details:
Connect the UI to the query/serving API: typed query clients per metric, request cancellation, caching of identical queries within a session, and consistent loading / error / empty / stale states for every chart.

Include retry-with-backoff on transient failures and a visible "data as of" timestamp driven by the pipeline's freshness metadata.

Done when: dashboards render live data in staging, and a forced API error shows a recoverable error state instead of a blank chart.

arguments.name: Compose the customer analytics dashboard page
arguments.details:
Assemble the approved customer page from library components and catalog metrics: customer counts, growth/cohort trend, segment breakdown, and the top-customer table.

Use a responsive grid so the page reflows from desktop to tablet widths, and keep the metric-to-visual mapping identical to the wireframes.

Done when: the page matches the approved wireframe, all values trace to the catalog, and stakeholder review feedback is addressed.

arguments.name: Compose the operations and log analytics page
arguments.details:
Assemble the operations page: request volume, error rate split by 4xx/5xx, latency percentiles, top error signatures, and endpoint drill-down entry points, all from the log aggregates.

Include a compact incident banner area that surfaces currently firing anomaly alerts rather than only historical charts.

Done when: the page renders live log aggregates, alert state shows correctly, and it matches the approved wireframe.

arguments.name: Implement global filters, date range and drill-down
arguments.details:
Add the cross-cutting interaction model: a global date-range control with sensible presets, segment/service/environment filters that apply to all charts on a page, and drill-down from an aggregate to its underlying detail table.

State must be reflected in the URL so a filtered view can be shared or bookmarked. Requests are debounced and only the visible charts refetch.

Done when: a filtered, drilled-down URL restored in a new tab reproduces exactly the same view.

arguments.name: Accessibility, responsive and frontend performance pass
arguments.details:
One consolidated hardening pass, timeboxed: keyboard navigation and focus order, screen-reader labels and table alternatives for every chart, colour-contrast check on the palette, and behavior at mobile/tablet breakpoints.

Performance: verify the initial dashboard load against the agreed budget, lazy-load below-the-fold charts, and keep the chart bundle out of the critical path.

Done when: an automated accessibility scan is clean on both pages, and load time in staging is within budget.

arguments.name: Design the analytics data model and storage layout
arguments.details:
Produce the schema that both pipelines write into and the dashboard reads from: raw/landing layer, normalized event and customer tables, and pre-aggregated rollup tables for charts.

Specify keys, partitioning and sort strategy (by date and high-cardinality dimension), retention per layer, and which queries each rollup serves. Include a short written rationale for warehouse choice and expected cost at current volumes.

Done when: DDL for all layers is committed and reviewed by both the data and frontend owners.

arguments.name: Provision dev, staging and production environments
arguments.details:
Create the three environments with infrastructure-as-code: storage/warehouse instances, compute for the ingestion and aggregation jobs, the query/API service, and the frontend hosting.

Wire up networking, least-privilege service identities per component, and environment-specific configuration. Keep them reproducible from code - no console-only changes.

Done when: a clean `apply` builds all three environments from scratch and each passes a connectivity smoke test.

arguments.name: Implement orchestration and job scheduling
arguments.details:
Schedule the CSV ingestion, log parsing and aggregation jobs with explicit dependencies and retry policy: CSV load runs on file arrival, log aggregation on a fixed cadence, rollups after their inputs complete.

Include run history, per-task retries with backoff, concurrency limits so backfills do not starve scheduled runs, and a manual trigger/backfill entry point for operators.

Done when: a full daily cycle runs unattended in staging for three consecutive days with no manual intervention.

arguments.name: Add authentication and role-based access control
arguments.details:
Put the dashboard behind SSO and map identity to roles (viewer, analyst, admin) that control page visibility, drill-down to row-level customer detail, and export rights.

Enforce authorization in the query API as well as the UI, and make sure row-level customer data is only returned to roles entitled to it.

Done when: each role is verified with a test account, and a direct API call bypassing the UI is correctly rejected.

arguments.name: Set up CI/CD for build, test and deploy
arguments.details:
One pipeline covering all components: lint and unit tests on pull request, integration tests on merge, and promotion to staging then production behind a manual approval.

Include schema migration handling with rollback, artifact versioning so a deploy is traceable to a commit, and a documented rollback procedure.

Done when: a trivial change flows from PR to staging automatically, and a deliberate failing test blocks the merge.

arguments.name: Run end-to-end integration testing across all three streams
arguments.details:
Exercise the full path in staging: drop a fresh customer CSV and confirm it appears on the customer dashboard; generate known synthetic log traffic and confirm error rate, latency and volume match the injected truth; verify alert rules fire.

Cover the nasty paths too - a malformed CSV, a late-arriving log batch, and a full re-run - and record results in a test matrix.

Done when: the test matrix is fully green and any accepted deviations are written down with owners.

arguments.name: Add job and pipeline observability with alert routing
arguments.details:
Instrument every scheduled job with success/failure/duration metrics, and expose freshness indicators for each layer the dashboard depends on. Define what "the dashboard is stale" means numerically.

Route alerts to the team's channel with clear ownership, and add a simple status view showing last successful run per job.

Done when: a failed job and a stale table each raise exactly one routed alert within the agreed detection window.

arguments.name: Write the runbook and hold launch readiness review
arguments.details:
Document the operational essentials: how to trigger a backfill, how to recover a failed load, how to rotate credentials, who owns each job, and what to do when a data-quality check fails. Keep it short and task-oriented.

Then run a go/no-go review against the milestone exit criteria with stakeholders, listing open risks, known limitations and the post-launch support plan.

Done when: the runbook is published and linked from the alert messages, and go/no-go is signed off.

arguments.name: Implement field-level mapping and type normalization
arguments.details:
Scope narrowed to structural mapping only. For each validated raw column: target analytics column, cast/parse rule, UTC date normalization, text trimming and case rules, currency and country-code standardization, and explicit handling for unmapped or unexpected columns.

Leave derived attributes (tenure bands, lifecycle flags) and test coverage out of this task - they are separate sibling tasks.

Done when: a fixture file loads through the mapping to the analytics customer table with no unmapped column present in the source.

arguments.name: Define the customer business key and conflict rules
arguments.details:
Decision task, no production code. Write down: the business key that identifies one customer across all exports, the precedence when the same customer appears in overlapping files (most recent snapshot vs most complete record), how soft-deletes are represented, and which fields may never be overwritten by a stale file.

Get sign-off from the owner of the customer data. This spec is what the following upsert and change-detection tasks implement.

Done when: the rules are written in the repo with worked examples for three conflicting-record cases.

arguments.name: Implement derived customer attributes
arguments.details:
Add the computed fields the dashboard needs on top of the mapped customer table: tenure band from signup date, active/churned flag from last-activity date, and any segment bucket agreed in the metric catalog.

Each attribute gets a one-line written definition and must be computed deterministically from the stored source fields so it can be recalculated by a backfill.

Done when: derived fields are populated on the full fixture set and their definitions appear in the data dictionary.

arguments.name: Unit-test the customer transformation on fixtures
arguments.details:
Write the test suite that locks down mapping and derived-attribute behavior: one case per source file, plus targeted cases for mixed date formats, currency symbols, blank optional fields and unknown columns.

Tests must run against the saved fixtures in CI, not against production data.

Done when: the suite covers every mapping rule and fails loudly if a mapping is removed or a derived definition changes.

arguments.name: Implement upsert, merge and soft-delete handling
arguments.details:
Implement the write path that enforces the signed-off business key and conflict rules: upsert by key, field-level precedence on conflict, and soft-delete marking so a customer disappears from the dashboard without losing history.

Must be safe to run concurrently with a scheduled load, so use a transactional or merge-based write rather than read-then-insert.

Done when: replaying a file twice, then loading a newer snapshot with a changed field and a removed customer, leaves exactly one row per customer with the expected values and delete state.

arguments.name: Add unchanged-file change detection
arguments.details:
Compute a content hash per incoming file and store it alongside the load record so an identical re-delivery is skipped instead of reparsed and rewritten.

Log the skip explicitly (file, hash, previous load time) so operators can tell "skipped as duplicate" apart from "failed to appear".

Done when: re-dropping an already-processed file produces a logged skip with zero writes to the customer table.

cells.question: I need to launch a new analytics dashboard project that includes data processing from our customer CSV files, log analysis from our application logs, and visualization components. Can you help me structure the major milestones and break them down into manageable tasks, making sure we don't have any tasks that are too complex to execute?
cells.answer:
Done. Here's the structure that now exists in the workspace.

## Project: Customer Analytics Dashboard
`a1839f20-0437-457a-b639-5d3e0017aa7b` — 4 milestones, 32 executable tasks (36 records total).

**M1: Customer CSV Data Pipeline** (10 tasks, 73h) — exit: any new CSV drop is validated, transformed and queryable with no manual steps; rejects quarantined with reasons.
- Profile sources & schema contract (3) → CSV ingestion loader (4) → row validation + bad-row quarantine (4) → field-level mapping + type normalization (3) → derived attributes (3) → business key & conflict rules (2) → upsert/merge/soft-delete (4) → unchanged-file change detection (2) → transformation unit tests (2) → data-quality checks & failure reporting (3)

**M2: Application Log Analysis** (6 tasks, 69h) — exit: metrics on a schedule, reconciled to source logs, one validated alert rule.
- Log source inventory (2) → parse/normalize to structured events (5) → metric definitions (2) → error-rate/latency/volume aggregates (5) → anomaly detection & alert rules (5) → reconcile against source logs (3)

**M3: Visualization & Dashboard UI** (8 tasks, 104h) — exit: approved dashboard within latency budget, keyboard accessible, every chart traced to the catalog.
- Metric catalog + wireframes (3) → app scaffold/tokens (3) → chart component library (5) → data-fetching layer (4) → customer page (4) → operations page (4) → filters/date-range/drill-down (4) → a11y, responsive & performance pass (4)

**M4: Platform Foundations & Production Launch** (8 tasks, 110h) — exit: all three streams running together in staging, role-gated, runbook published, go/no-go signed.
- Data model & storage layout (5) → environments (4) → orchestration/scheduling (5) → auth & RBAC (4) → CI/CD (4) → E2E integration testing (5) → job observability & alert routing (4) → runbook + launch review (3)

## Complexity verification
I ran `analyze_task_complexity` at threshold 7 twice. The first pass flagged two leaf tasks at 7/10 (*"Transform validated rows…"* and *"Handle deduplication, identity matching and re-delivered files"* — both flagged for long names and multi-concern descriptions). I split them rather than relabeling: the transformation became mapping/normalization + derived attributes + a fixture test suite; dedup became a business-key decision task + upsert/merge implementation + change detection.

Second pass: **32 of 36 tasks are below 7, average 4.8/10, max leaf complexity 5.** The only remaining ≥7 items are the four milestone records themselves (8/9), which are epic containers with children — not work anyone executes directly. The analyzer scores M3/M4 at 9 purely from description length; I left that score honest rather than lowering it to quiet the report.

Two practical notes: the `list_tasks` tree view repeats child tasks in its flat tail section, so it reports 68 — the analysis tool's count of 36 is the real total. And the hour estimates (356h total, ~9 weeks serial / ~4-5 weeks across 3-4 parallel tracks) are sizing placeholders, not commitments — worth replacing once M1's profiling and M2's log inventory land, since those two discovery tasks are what actually determine the downstream effort.
